title: Partition full Python and WebView discovery
summary: Run the complete Python and WebView unittest roots sequentially in hosted CI so browser/CDP suites do not inherit thousands of unrelated tests in the same Python process.
reason: Four hosted full-discovery attempts failed on different browser modules after more than 500 seconds, while every unchanged module and the full 29-test browser suite passed independently. A single long-lived discovery process accumulates browser/subprocess pressure and produces non-deterministic wait failures.
behavior_before: Deep Audit and Generated Drift each ran all 3,139 tests in one Python process with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -q`; late browser/CDP tests failed non-deterministically on different waits.
behavior_after: Each workflow still discovers every test under tests/python and tests/webview, in that order, but uses a fresh Python process for the WebView root. No test, assertion, browser timeout, workflow permission, or required context is removed or weakened.
manual_validation: PASS: identical partitioned discovery locally; tests/python and tests/webview both passed, preserving all 3,139 tests with one expected skip.
PASS: full tests/webview root passed 239 tests, including all 29 browser-backed tests.
PASS: every browser module that failed in hosted aggregate discovery passed unchanged in local isolated/full-browser runs.

OBSERVED: hosted failures rotated across Launch/Queue, Diagnostics handoff, Settings/Launch, Rename, Completed/Pending proof, and High Risk, demonstrating process-lifetime/resource sensitivity rather than one product assertion.
rollback_plan: Restore the single discovery command only if a future runner proves it stable under equivalent browser load. Do not compensate by increasing timeouts or skipping browser tests.
notes: The required check names and workflow permissions are unchanged. This is execution isolation within each existing Python unit-test job, not a reduction in test scope.
